title: Draft legislation: Plastic packaging tax — chemical recycling and adoption of a mass balance approach - GOV.UK

triage.reason: GOV.UK published a technical consultation on draft Plastic Packaging Tax regulations for chemical recycling and mass balance accounting, seeking views on legislation due to apply from 1 April 2027.

draft.summary: On 6 October 2026, draft Regulations and a draft reference document on chemical recycling and adoption of a mass balance approach for Plastic Packaging Tax were published for technical consultation. The draft Regulations set out the conditions that businesses must meet to use a mass balance approach to account for chemically recycled plastic from 1 April 2027, including certification, auditing, monitoring and record-keeping requirements.
draft.source_quote: The draft Regulations set out the conditions that businesses must meet if they wish to use a mass balance approach to account for chemically recycled plastic for Plastic Packaging Tax (PPT) purposes from 1 April 2027. The draft reference document sets out the methodology for applying dual-use factors where required. Both should be read alongside the relevant provisions of the Finance Act 2021, as amended by the Finance Act 2026, in particular sections 49, 49A and 49B.

key_dates.text: The draft Regulations set out conditions for businesses to use a mass balance approach to account for chemically recycled plastic for Plastic Packaging Tax purposes from 1 April 2027.

draft.interpretation: This may require recyclers and converters using chemically recycled plastic to obtain certification and comply with mass-balance audit and record-keeping rules before accounting for it for Plastic Packaging Tax purposes from 1 April 2027.
